function.name: analyze_dna_sequence
function.description: Analyzes the DNA sequence based on a reference sequence and return any potential mutations. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

sequence.description: The DNA sequence to be analyzed.

mutation_type.description: Type of the mutation to be looked for in the sequence.

message.content:
**Analysis of the two query sequences against the reference “AGCTTAGCTA”**

| Sequence | Mutation type examined | Result |
|----------|------------------------|--------|
| **AGCTTAGCTA** | *Insertion* | Identical to the reference – no additional nucleotides were detected. |
| **AGCTTAGGCTA** | *Insertion* | One extra ‘G’ appears immediately after the seventh base of the reference. Thus an insertion occurs at position 8 (ref‑base numbering starts at 1). |

---

### Deletion Analysis  
A deletion would mean fewer bases than the reference. Neither of the supplied sequences lacks any nucleotide compared to the reference, so **no deletions** are observed in either case.

### Substitution Analysis  
Substitutions involve changing a base while keeping overall length constant.

| Sequence | Comparison | Observation |
|----------|------------|-------------|
| **AGCTTAGCTA** | Same as reference | No mismatches → no substitutions. |
| **AGCTTAGGCTA** | Length differs by +1 → alignment shows all matching except for the added ‘G’. When aligning the overlapping region, every base matches the reference exactly. Therefore **no substitutions** are identified. |

> **Summary:**  
> - **Sequence 1 (“AGCTTAGCTA”)**: perfectly matches the reference—no insertions, deletions, or substitutions.  
> - **Sequence 2 (“AGCTTAGGCTA”)**: contains a single insertion (extra ‘G’) at position 8; otherwise it aligns identically to the reference, yielding no deletions or replacements.
